minors.title: The probe-section call in _check_raw_sections is unreachable, so its tailored message never appears
minors.detail: In _check_raw_sections (fixed file lines 525-534) the allowed-sections loop runs first and raises for any key not in _yaml_allowed_sections(workflow). Under a workflow containing inject, 'probe' maps to stage train and is never allowed, so that loop raises "probe: no stage of this file's workflow reads this section" before the second loop's `if 'probe' in d: _refuse_probe_under_inject(workflow, 'probe')` is ever reached. C4's 'probe section under inject' line confirms it: the message is the allowed-sections one, not the probe-under-inject one. The models.probe call two lines below is live (models is an always-section), so only the probe-section call is dead. The deadness predates this round (the old code had the same shape in the same spot) and the diff restructured exactly those lines without removing it; either drop the dead call or move the probe-under-inject check ahead of the allowed-sections loop so a probe: section under inject gets the message that explains why.

minors.title: The whole-call-generator gate compares a bool to False instead of stating the condition
minors.detail: Lines 895-896 read `whole_call_generator = gen_kind == 'generator' and checkpoint_meta.get('param_only') is False` then `if whole_call_generator is False:`. The variable is already a bool, so `is False` is a spelled-out negation of an affirmative name; the repo's rule is to write the condition in the affirmative and negate once (`if not whole_call_generator:`). The identity comparison also makes the gate type-strict in a way nothing asked for: a method file whose CHECKPOINT_META writes `param_only: 0` would be refused, since `0 is False` is false in Python, while `param_only: false` passes. No method file in the tree writes 0, so nothing is broken today; both lines are new in this round's diff.

How each finding was fixed at its root:
- SCHEMA-2 / SCHEMA-3: the wrong logic was the order inside _finalize. The environment-dependent checks (data.instructions against INSTRUCTIONS, the per-element split check against the splits block and SPLIT_ROLE), the model checks (role, family lookup, generation.effort against EFFORTS), _resolve_generation and the model-row expansion now all run after _apply_inheritance, on the values inheritance chose. Nothing was wrapped or special-cased.
- SCHEMA-4: one function _refuse_probe_under_inject(workflow, dotted) is now the refusal, called from the raw-file check, the command-line override loop, the sweep field list, and _finalize over the merged setting (full["models"]["probe"] is not None), each naming the dotted field. The _finalize guard sits before the role check so the message is the probe-under-inject one, not an accidental "not a row of models/table.yaml".
- Owner ruling: _resolve_ref returns (kind, payload, method); _pinned_method requires method: on inject.probe_score/inject.probe_gen in the key:/dir: forms, refuses it on eval.theta_from and score.baseline and on a name-form reference, and checks it against AXES["probe.method"]. _substitute fills {probe_score_method} from it and the whole-call-generator check reads it for all three forms.

How _resolve_ref validates the stage set, as asked: it compares set(value[kind]) -- the INNER dict under key:/dir: -- against _ref_requirements(field), read off the stage table's upstream cells (train+eval for probe_score, train for probe_gen). method: is a sibling of key:/dir: at the outer level, so it can never be taken for a stage. The method also never enters the fields block: fields_of skips all four REF_FIELDS, so the whole reference value stays out, and the method reaches the key only through versions as eval/methods/<m>.py (proved: fields block is ['inject.theta']).

Decisions the findings and the ruling did not make (all in the report):
1. The type check and the axis/RETIRED check stay ahead of _apply_inheritance: they validate what this file states, an inherited value already passed the same axis check when its own setting loaded, and moving them past reference resolution would turn C4's "probe.method: 'ctoool' is not one of (...)" into a FileNotFoundError from _method_kind.
2. A pinned reference's outer entries are closed to {key|dir, method}; an unknown sibling is refused by name instead of ignored.
3. The name-form refusal is implemented as "a mapping carrying method: with neither key: nor dir: is refused, naming the field", since a name reference is a plain <workflow>/<setting> string and a sibling cannot be attached to one any other way.
4. inject.probe_gen's gate now reads CHECKPOINT_META param_only is False (the ruling's words) rather than the previous falsy test, so a method file that omits param_only is refused, naming it.
5. _refuse_probe_under_inject's single message changed the text of C4's models.probe-under-inject line; the field it names is unchanged.

D2's last assertion, as instructed, is reported as a known script defect: the ticket's D2 never snapshots the train key before editing trainer.py -- both S.key('train', c) and S.key('train', c2) are evaluated inside the same print, after the edit, and key() reads every VERSION off disk on each call (3.3), so two identical settings keyed against the same current disk state are equal by 3.2 rule 1. Output is "False True"; with the snapshot taken first the same sub-test gives "True True". No code change was made for it.

Not done, deliberately: M-G3 (the real-tree rerun without the fixture) needs eval/methods/, which lands in a later wave; baseline.yaml already loads against the real tree.

minors.title: _stays_one_argument rejects a bare value whose bracket depth dips below zero and returns to zero, so build_call refuses values it could write
minors.detail: The new `_stays_one_argument` (data/environments/appworld.py:155-182) returns False the moment `brackets` goes negative. The guard is needed for a value whose depth *ends* negative (a lone `]` would swallow the following argument), but that case is already caught by the closing `brackets == 0` check, and the mid-string form also rejects a value that dips below zero and comes back to zero, which the reader it models handles correctly. Measured on an export of a1e61c6 with probe-env python: value `(})[\` gives `_closes_the_call` True, `_stays_one_argument` False, so `_bare_safe` is False; the quoting branch then dies on the trailing backslash and `build_call` raises ValueError, while the bare writing round-trips under this same head, alone (`apis.a.b(k=(})[\)` -> `[('k', '(})[\\')]`) and beside a second argument (`apis.a.b(k=(})[\, m=x)` -> `[('k', '(})[\\'), ('m', 'x')]`; `_split_args_named('k=(})[\, m=x')` keeps both). The base 511e61d wrote this value correctly, so it is a regression introduced by this round: in my 139,910-write fuzz, 2 writes (one value, under both key kinds) go from ok at 511e61d to ValueError at a1e61c6, and 108 distinct values are refused although a bare writing round-trips for this reason (a further 115 are the `=`-rule class the report's Decisions item 2 already hands to the owner). Weighting: the refusal is loud and names tool, key and value, no corpus value is affected (0 of 5,297 argument values hold a backslash), and the same diff removes 10,310 silent mis-writes, so this is a completeness gap in `build_call` as the inverse of `split_args`, not a correctness hazard. Root-cause shape if it is worth closing: make the guard the rule the reader actually has (a value whose bracket depth ends below zero, or that carries a `,` or `=` where the reader's depth is zero) rather than any dip.

Section 2, `build_call`'s quoting rule, "wrap the value in a quote when it is empty, holds a top-level `,` or `=`, or ends with an unbalanced bracket or quote": the rule as written has no answer for a value that needs quoting and ends in an odd number of backslashes — no writing represents it under the ticket's own `.strip().strip("\"'")` parse rule (proved exhaustively this round), so `build_call` raises `ValueError` naming the tool, the key and the value, the same way the ticket's both-quote-kinds case does. 0 of the 5,297 argument values of the p1 corpus hold a backslash at all, so no real trajectory reaches it.
notes:
Decisions the findings did not make, all in the report:
1. The writer asks the reader rather than gaining one more copied rule. Copying _call_close's escape rule into _bare_safe would have kept the copy that produced ENV-3; _bare_safe and _quote_value now call _call_close itself. That is why the fuzz's broken column is 0 over 109,999 values: the writer writes no call the reader reads back as something else.
2. A value that needs quoting and ends in an odd number of backslashes is refused by name instead of written unparsable, the same choice the ticket already makes for a value holding both quote kinds. One case inside that class, 'a=b\', is writable bare, and it is refused with the rest: the ticket's quoting rule quotes on any top-level ',' or '=' regardless of the key, while the reader reads a key off the first '=' alone. I built the key-aware version, measured it and reverted it — it rescues that class but contradicts the ticket's stated quoting rule and rewrites 7 real corpus actions (password='ZEgU=ep' becomes password=ZEgU=ep). Relaxing the '=' rule for a named key is the owner's call.
3. A value that begins or ends with a quote character is still left alone (round 1's measured reason: the ticket's .strip().strip("\"'") preserves no such value under any writing, and split_args produces none — 0 of 5,297 corpus values).
4. README.md untouched: no import added, nothing read or written, same venv, so the five annotation lines are unchanged.
